title: Out-of-equilibrium inhomogeneous XX chains: Exact results and the hydrodynamic limit
abstract: We study the out-of-equilibrium dynamics in the XX chain with step-like magnetic field, which maps to an inhomogeneous tight-binding chain after Jordan-Wigner transformation. We obtain exact analytic expressions for the fermionic two-point correlation function after a quantum quench from several initial product states, both homogeneous and inhomogeneous ones. This is achieved by using a combination of Fourier and Laplace transforms, which al low us to map the problem to a standard Riemann-Hilbert problem on the unit circle. For arbitrary positions and times the correlators are not expressed in terms of elementary functions. However, in the hydrodynamic limit $x,y,t\to\infty$ with fixed ratios, we provide explicit formulas that depend only on the effective transmission coefficient across the origin. We benchmark our analytic predictions against exact numerical simulations and find excellent agreement in the hydrodynamic limit, apart from finite-time corrections.
summary: This paper derives exact analytical solutions for the out-of-equilibrium dynamics of an inhomogeneous XX chain following a quantum quench. By mapping the problem to a Riemann-Hilbert formulation, the authors provide explicit formulas for correlation functions, especially in the asymptotic hydrodynamic limit. This advances the theoretical understanding of non-equilibrium transport in structured quantum many-body systems.
main_problem: The study focuses on determining the exact out-of-equilibrium dynamics of fermionic correlation functions following a quantum quench in an inhomogeneous XX chain.
main_result: Exact analytic expressions for two-point correlation functions are derived using Riemann-Hilbert methods, yielding explicit formulas in the hydrodynamic limit that match numerical simulations.
method: The problem is mapped to a Riemann-Hilbert problem on the unit circle via Fourier and Laplace transforms, allowing for an exact analytical solution of the fermionic correlation function.
model_or_system: The system is the XX chain subjected to a step-like magnetic field, which maps to an inhomogeneous tight-binding chain described by a quadratic fermionic Hamiltonian. The dynamics are studied after quenching from various initial product states.
key_observables: Two-point fermionic correlation function Gxy(t), reflection (R) and transmission (T) amplitudes across the inhomogeneity.
important_parameters: The hydrodynamic limit ($x, y, t 	o \infty$ with fixed ratios); magnetic field strengths ($h_L, h_R$).
main_assumptions: For the dynamics, the solution relies on factorizing the correlation matrix and solving the resulting integral equation via RHP techniques.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the setup of the inhomogeneous chain and show numerical data for the fermionic correlator |Gxy| compared against the derived hydrodynamic limit result.
paper_structure: The paper proceeds by first analyzing single-particle scattering to find transmission/reflection coefficients, then deriving the dynamics of the correlation matrix using linear equations of motion, solving this via a Riemann-Hilbert problem, and finally presenting results in both finite time and the asymptotic hydrodynamic limit.
why_interesting: This work provides rigorous analytical tools (RHP) to calculate non-equilibrium observables like correlations across interfaces, which is crucial for understanding energy/information transport in structured quantum materials.

We consider the inhomogeneous tight-binding chain with two different magnetic fields (chemical potentials) hL and hR in the two semi- infinite halves of the chain. We consider unitary dynamics from several initial states. The figure shows the inhomogeneous N´eel state in which the right-half of the chain is prepared in the N´eel state and the left part is in the fermionic vacuum state.
